explanation: Noodles are not a traditional staple of Brazilian cuisine, but general table manners there follow Western/European conventions favoring quiet, closed-mouth eating. Audible slurping — of noodles, soup, or coffee — is typically seen as a minor lapse in manners rather than a serious offense, especially outside formal settings.
local_tip: When eating noodle dishes (increasingly common via Japanese-Brazilian and Italian-Brazilian food culture), eat quietly as you would any other dish — slurping isn't expected or appreciated.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is a sign of enjoyment and appreciation for the dish.
Slurping is common and signals you're savoring the meal, though very loud slurping can seem crude in formal settings.
Slurping pasta is considered quite uncivilized; quiet, deliberate eating is the norm.
